text:
elaine: Quick check — ran the lytic13b quant sweep last night (int8, int6, int4) against our longform summarization slice. Summary in the table below, need recommendations for product traffic split and a short GTN note.

sam: awesome, can you paste the key numbers?

elaine: sure — short version: int8 keeps quality ~neutral on ROUGE & human spot-checks, gives ~28% token-cost savings; int6 gets ~35% savings but a subtle loss on long-context coherence (~+0.9 pts ROUGE-L drop); int4 saves ~52% but shows hallucination spikes on certain prompts. latency tail improves proportionally: p95 down ~18% (int8) / 30% (int6) / 46% (int4).

kai: do we have per-token cost math? also which prompts caused hallucination in int4?

elaine: per-token rough (incl infra amort): fp16 baseline = $0.012/token, int8 = $0.0086, int6 = $0.0078, int4 = $0.0058. Hallucination mostly on multi-document synth prompts where the model compresses citations (seen on slice "multi-article-merge").

nora: thanks. Any eval numbers vs baseline on the signal slice? even small BLEU/ROUGE diffs matter for GTN.

elaine: quick excerpt of the scorecard we used:
```
slice: longform-news-merge | baseline(fp16) | int8 | int6 | int4
ROUGE-L: 41.2 | 40.9 (-0.3) | 40.1 (-1.1) | 38.7 (-2.5)
Human pass rate (clarity/faith): 88% | 86% | 81% | 67%
Latency p95 (ms): 420 | 344 | 294 | 225
Cost per 1k tokens ($): 12.0 | 8.6 | 7.8 | 5.8
```

sam: interesting tradeoffs. For GTN / product guidance, we need a recommended traffic split and a short note for sales (so they can set expectations).

kai: my thinking: default hosted should land on int8 with fallback to fp16 for flagged prompts. Keep int6 for dedicated reserved pools where customers opt-in for higher savings and accept minor fidelity loss. Int4 should be experimental — gated behind canary + strict QA and only for very price-sensitive tiers.

elaine: agree. Also suggest we add a priming-based routing rule: if the incoming prompt matches our "multi-article-merge" or includes >3 documents, route to fp16 or int8 with KV cache warmstart to avoid int4 issues. We can detect that by tokenized source_count > 3.

nora: can we quantify the customer-facing upsell messaging? maybe: "low-cost tier: up to 50% cost reduction with optional quality tradeoffs; recommended for short Q&A/embeddings, not for multi-doc summarization." Thoughts?

sam: that's good. For GTN one-pager: put the numbers for int8 as our recommended balance (28% saving, ~0.3 ROUGE drop, p95 improved). Then note int6 as opt-in for dedicated customers and int4 as lab/POC only. Call out the multi-doc regression specifically.

ops-bot: deploy-check: rolling-canary for int8 config scheduled 2025-06-10T03:00Z, owner @elaine.

elaine: I'll push the rollout plan: canary at 1% traffic on hosted, monitor rouge & human-flag rate; if human-flag rate > +2% vs baseline on the slice for 1h, auto-rollback. Also will add a routing rule to divert identified multi-doc prompts to fp16.

kai: suggest adding a synthetic adversarial prompt set for int4 if we ever pursue it — capture hallucination triggers so we don't surprise buyers.

nora: can you draft the 3-line GTN blurb and share? product wants to include it in the upcoming partner deck.

elaine: draft below — feedback welcome: 
"Lytic-13B cost-performance: int8 recommended (≈28% cost reduction with minimal quality impact on single-doc tasks). Int6 provides deeper savings for dedicated/reserved deployments with modest quality tradeoffs. Int4 yields largest cost savings but currently shows hallucination risk on multi-document summarization — recommended for experimental/lab usage only. Route multi-doc prompts to fp16/int8 to preserve faithfulness."

sam: short and clear. Add a one-line note: "Canary plan: hosted int8 at 1% -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback on quality regressions."

elaine: added. I'll upload the slice-level scorecard + logs to the run-tracker and tag the GTN draft. Leaving this thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
